LESSON: WRITING 1.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should one be careful when filling in forms?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the required information to be filled in forms for different purposes

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 1.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 1.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the required information to be filled in forms for different purposes

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the required information to be filled in forms for different purposes. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the required information to be filled in forms for different purposes.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the required information to be filled in forms for different purposes. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the required information to be filled in forms for different purposes)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the required information to be filled in forms for different purposes.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should one be careful when filling in forms?
2. What information do we fill in forms?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the required information to be filled in forms for different purposes.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
